mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and thus producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the horizon are positive with a p-value < 0.05 in a two-tailed test against the pre-trend mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in labor market participation (PAYEMS and UNRATE) creates a dual signal of weakening demand, which depresses consumer confidence and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by >5% while UNRATE increases by >0.5 percentage points within the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) when using the same proxies as triggers.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 4% in a month indicates excess demand that the market anticipates will persist, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 4% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is negative or not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when controlling for lagged inflation (CPIAUCSL).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 for two consecutive months suggests supply-side weakness that lags into equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive with a Sharpe ratio exceeding the 12-month equity risk premium.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 3.5% and coincides with a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL < 3%), it triggers a dual signal of labor market tightening and cooling price pressures that the Fed interprets as a 'soft landing,' associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% and CPIAUCSL < 3.0% in the same month
regime_hint: labor market tightening with cooling inflation
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative with a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining worker participation in the labor force (UNRATE > 0.5% increase over 3 months) reduces aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are consistently positive across 5 such regimes.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising short-term rates (FEDFUNDS) above 4% create a forward discounting effect that reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, producing negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive with a volatility-adjusted Sharpe ratio > 1.5.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a sustained rise in consumer confidence (implied by negative S&P 500 put options) creates a contrarian signal that the market underreacts to, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >8% in one month and S&P 500 put option volatility declines by >10% the following week
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) when using GARCH-modified t-tests for volatility adjustment.
